text:
maria: FYI customer INC-4821 reporting intermittent 503s when calling our hosted API over their AWS PrivateLink endpoint. Works fine from internet. Only their VPC -> privatelink path failing sometimes.

maria: Logs they pasted: curl https://api.redwood.example/v1/health -> sometimes returns 503, sometimes TLS handshake error. Paste: 
```
curl: (35) error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
{"error":"upstream unavailable"}
```

maya: Do we have their VPC endpoint ID? They mentioned VPCE but not ID. Need to confirm if they used Interface endpoint with private DNS on.

maria: They provided partial: vpce-0a12xxxx in us-east-1. Also said internal DNS resolves to the vpce hostname sometimes and to NLB IP other times. Their dig output: 
```
$ dig api.redwood.example +short
vpce-0a12abcd-xxxxxxxx.vpce-svc-xxxxxxxx.region.vpce.amazonaws.com.
10.0.12.45
```

ingrid: That smells like split-horizon + NLB healthcheck issues. NLB healthchecks originate from AWS IP ranges; if customer firewall blocks them intermittently the NLB will mark targets unhealthy and return 502/503.

ingrid: Also need to check whether NLB is doing TLS termination vs passthrough. If NLB listener is TLS and targets expect TLS from client, SNI/host header mismatches can cause SSL errors.

maria: Customer says their firewall has a strict egress allowlist; they only allowed traffic to our public IP ranges, but PrivateLink uses ENIs in their subnet so source/dest IPs differ. They might have outbound rules blocking the NLB healthcheck IPs.

maya: Quick repro steps for infra: 1) Create an interface VPC endpoint for our service in a test VPC. 2) Enable private DNS for api.redwood.example. 3) From a VM in the VPC, curl the endpoint repeatedly under simulated firewall drop of AWS healthcheck IPs. 4) Observe 503s and intermittent TLS errors.

maya: Config checks: - Ensure NLB listener protocol is TCP if we want passthrough, or TLS if we terminate on NLB but then cert SAN must match vpce hostname. - Confirm customer firewall allows AWS healthcheck ranges or specifically allows VPCE ENI IPs and NLB health IPs.

maria: Customer attached tcpdump snippet showing client -> vpce ENI -> NLB: SYN, SYN-ACK, TLS ClientHello, then RST sometimes.

eng-infra-bot: Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/privatelink-nlb-troubleshoot (check healthcheck sources, listener mode, private DNS)

ingrid: Suggested immediate mitigations to ask customer: 1) Temporarily allow the AWS region healthcheck IP ranges (we can provide list) or loosen egress to allow ENI->NLB traffic. 2) If using TLS, switch NLB to TCP passthrough to avoid SNI issues, or upload cert to NLB with proper SANs. 3) Confirm private DNS is resolving consistently to VPCE CNAME and not directly to NLB public IP.

maria: I asked them to run `aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=attachment.instance-owner-id,Values=vpce*` to map ENIs and adjust firewall rules. They ran it and gave ENI IPs.

maria: Can eng-infra supply the exact healthcheck source CIDRs for the NLB so they can allow them?

ingrid: I'll pull the AWS healthcheck CIDRs for us-east-1 and paste. Also confirm our NLB is configured with TCP listener on port 443 for the PrivateLink service (we do TCP passthrough currently) — that reduces TLS mismatch risk.

maya: If they keep seeing TLS errors after allowing healthchecks, ask for a packet capture showing ClientHello and server response, plus `openssl s_client -connect <eni-ip>:443 -servername api.redwood.example -tls1_2` output.

maria: Customer will try allowing CIDRs and report back. Ticket updated INC-4821. Adding eng-infra for follow-up. :thumbsup:
